title: totalenergies eni approve cyprus gas field lng 2028 startup 2026 07 28
text:
PARIS/MILAN, July 28 (Reuters) - France's ​TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA)
, opens new tab
 and Italy's Eni (ENI.MI)
, opens new tab
 have approved the development of ‌the Cronos gas field in Cyprus to supply Europe with liquefied natural gas, with production start-up expected in 2028, TotalEnergies said ​on Tuesday.
The 2.8 million metric tons of LNG per ​year expected from the field will be marketed ⁠equally between the two companies.
European countries have shown growing interest ​in exploiting domestic resources after losing access to Russian oil and ​gas in the wake of the Ukraine war in 2022 and now as they face import disruptions from the war in Iran.
Cronos is a major ​natural gas discovery in Block 6 of Cyprus' exclusive ​economic zone in the Mediterranean Sea, operated as a 50/50 joint ‌venture ⁠between operator Eni and TotalEnergies.
Estimated to hold more than 3 trillion cubic feet of gas, the project plans to pipe and process the reserves in Eni's existing facilities in Egypt ​for export towards ​Europe via ⁠the Damietta LNG terminal.
"As Cyprus’ first gas project, Cronos will support the development of a new ​regional gas hub in the Eastern Mediterranean, ​leveraging Egypt’s ⁠infrastructure," TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanne said in a statement.
"This new gas route in the Mediterranean will contribute to Europe’s ⁠energy security ​by diversifying its LNG supply ​sources," he added.
